title: Container Bookings: Holding Several Bookings at Once
content:
Aurelia Hanse Line sets no limit on how many Container Bookings a single customer may keep open simultaneously.

## Policy clause

A customer may hold as many bookings concurrently as it wishes; the number of live bookings per customer is uncapped. Each booking stands as a holding in its own right, with a charge account and a lifecycle belonging to it alone. The ceiling on containers is a limit on each booking individually, and it is set by the admission rules for a booking request. A shipper may divide one shipment across several bookings, and each of those bookings is then charged, amended, rolled and cancelled on its own, without regard to the others.

## The same clause, point by point

| Question | Answer under the clause |
|---|---|
| Is there a maximum number of live bookings per customer? | No; no such maximum exists. |
| Does a charge booked on one booking affect the account of another? | No; every booking keeps a separate charge account. |
| Is the container ceiling measured across all of a customer's bookings? | No; it applies booking by booking. |
| May one shipment be spread over several bookings? | Yes. |
| When one of those bookings is amended, rolled or cancelled, are the others touched? | No; each is handled independently. |

## Hypothetical illustration

A forwarder that already holds four live bookings on one trade lane asks for a fifth. The four existing bookings do not, by their number, stand in the way; the new request is judged on its own merits under the admission rules of the product requested. Should the forwarder later cancel one of the five, only that booking's own account bears whatever the cancellation brings. The booking counts in this illustration are invented.
